problem: What is the cardinality of $C\times D$ for $C={0,1,2,...,11}$ and $D={s,t,u,v}?$

examples.knowledge_point: Computing the Cardinality of a Cartesian Product
examples.problem: If $C = \{ 3, 4, 7, 9, 11 \}$ and $D  =\{ 1, 2, 3, \ldots, 10 \},$ what is the cardinality of $C \times D?$
examples.worked_solution:
For any two finite sets $C$ and $D,$ the cardinality of $C \times D$ is

$$
| C \times D | = |C| \cdot |D|.
$$

In this case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}|C\times D| & =|C|\cdot |D| \\  & =5\cdot 10 \\  & =50.\end{aligned}
$$

feedback.problem:
For the sets $X={5,10},$ $Y={r,s,t},$ and $Z=X\times Y,$ determine which of the following statements are true.

- $(5,r)\in Z$
- $(r,t)\in Z$
- $(10,s)\in Z$
feedback.worked_solution:
The Cartesian product $X\times Y$ consists of all ordered pairs whose first coordinate belongs to $X$ and whose second coordinate belongs to $Y.$

In this case, the schematic for $X\times Y$ is shown below.

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture-workers/linear/14040355/assets/1eb13d93fbefc4c7285edef537a9fb3e21339f7a3b37a179eeb150db8d726c1b.png)

Hence, the set $Z=X\times Y$ is given by

$$
Z={(5,r),(5,s),(5,t),(10,r),(10,s),(10,t)}.
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
